name: separator
description: A 1px rule used to visually divide content, with a margin axis (none/small/medium/large) controlling the space around the line and a direction axis (horizontal/vertical). Geometrically trivial: the visible line is a stroke-drawn RECTANGLE nested inside a padding-only wrapper frame. Reconciles the local `border-t border-klp-border-default` rule already used ad hoc by `calendar` (flagged there as a `new-primitive` gap) — both resolve to the same `--klp-border-default` alias, so `calendar` should be migrated to consume this component once adapted.

anatomy.notes: Padding-only wrapper. No visible fill or stroke of its own (transparent) — its sole job is reserving the margin space around the line via layout padding, which is direction-dependent: paddingTop/paddingBottom for Direction=Horizontal, paddingLeft/paddingRight for Direction=Vertical. `none` margin has zero padding (no Figma variable bound).

The actual visible rule. In Figma this is a RECTANGLE node named 'Rectangle 1' with a bound `strokes` entry (no `fills` entry at all — the node has zero fill paint). This means the rule is drawn as a STROKE, not a filled rectangle. Source must use `border-*` utilities (e.g. `border-b border-klp-border-default` for horizontal, `border-r border-klp-border-default` for vertical), never `bg-*`. strokeWeight is a literal 1 (not bound to a variable).

a11y.notes: Purely decorative divider by default — render with role="separator" and aria-orientation matching the direction axis ("horizontal" | "vertical"). Radix's react-separator handles this: when `decorative` is true it sets role="none" instead, which is preferable if the separator carries no semantic meaning for assistive tech (matches most usages, e.g. inside menus/calendars).
